chapterNote: Chapter 2 is a single sustained sentence — one long 'if... then' woven across twenty-two verses. IF the son will take in his father's words with the whole energy of a treasure-hunter (vv. 1-4), THEN he will gain the fear of the LORD and the very knowledge of God (vv. 5-8) and a trained moral discernment (vv. 9-11) — and that wisdom will rescue him from the two great threats to a young man: the perverse man with his twisted words and crooked company (vv. 12-15), and the seductive 'strange woman' whose smooth speech leads down to death (vv. 16-19). The end is a settled life on the good road, the upright dwelling in the land while the wicked are cut off (vv. 20-22).

1.text: My son, if you will receive my words and treasure up my commandments within you,
1.amp: My son, if you will receive [laqach — take to yourself, accept and hold] my words and treasure up [tsaphan — hide away, store as something precious] my commandments within you,
1.notes: tsaphan (H6845) is to hide something valuable, to store it like treasure — the same verb returns in v.7 for God's own storing of wisdom, and the hidden treasures of v.4 (matmon, from the kindred hiding-verb taman) keep the image in view. The son is to bury the father's words deep, where they cannot be lost. laqach (H3947) is more than hearing: it is taking wisdom into one's own possession.

2.text: so that you make your ear attentive to wisdom and bend your heart to understanding;
2.amp: so that you make your ear [ozen] attentive [qashab — prick up the ear, listen hard] to wisdom [chokmah], and incline [natah — stretch, bend toward] your heart to understanding [tebunah];
2.notes: qashab (H7181) is the alert, leaning-in listening of one who refuses to miss a word; natah (H5186) is to bend or stretch the heart deliberately toward understanding. Wisdom asks the whole posture of the body — ear and heart together, not one without the other. Other brackets: ozen (H241), chokmah (H2451), tebunah (H8394).

3.text: yes, if you call out for insight and lift up your voice for understanding,
3.amp: yes, if you cry out [qara — call aloud, summon] for insight [binah — discernment, the power to tell things apart] and lift up your voice for understanding [tebunah],
3.notes: binah (H998) is discernment, the trained ability to distinguish one thing from another. The doubled image — crying out, lifting the voice — makes the seeker as vocal and urgent for wisdom as Wisdom herself was for him in 1:20-21. Other brackets: qara (H7121), tebunah (H8394).

4.text: if you seek her like silver and search for her like buried treasure,
4.amp: if you seek [baqash — pursue, search after] her as silver [keseph], and search [chaphas — dig and ransack] for her as for hidden treasures [matmon];
4.notes: chaphas (H2664) is to search by digging and ransacking — the labor of a treasure-hunter; matmon (H4301) is buried treasure. Wisdom is not stumbled upon but mined: the same energy a man pours out to get rich, redirected to get wise. Other brackets: baqash (H1245), keseph (H3701).

5.text: then you will understand what it means to fear the LORD, and you will discover the knowledge of God.
5.amp: then you will understand [biyn — discern, grasp] what it is to fear the LORD [yirat YHWH] and discover [matsa — attain, light upon] the knowledge of God [daat Elohim].
5.notes: the long sentence reaches its first payoff: the reward of the wholehearted search (vv.1-4) is not mere cleverness but yirat YHWH (H3374 + H3068), the fear of the LORD — the same first principle as 1:7 — and the personal knowing (daat, H1847) of God Himself. Wisdom's true end is God. Other brackets: biyn (H995), matsa (H4672), Elohim (H430).

6.text: For it is the LORD who gives wisdom; from His mouth come knowledge and understanding.
6.amp: For the LORD gives [natan] wisdom [chokmah]; from His mouth [peh] come knowledge [daat] and understanding [tebunah].
6.notes: the search of vv.1-4 is real, yet wisdom is finally a gift, not a wage — it is given (natan, H5414) out of God's own mouth. The seeker digs, but what he finds was placed there by the Giver (cf. Jas 1:5). Knowledge and understanding are the very breath of God spoken toward man. Other brackets: chokmah (H2451), peh (H6310), daat (H1847), tebunah (H8394).

7.text: For the upright He lays away true wisdom; He is a shield over those whose walk is blameless,
7.amp: For the upright [yashar] He lays away [tsaphan — the same 'treasure up' of v.1, now God's own act] sound wisdom [tushiyyah — competent wisdom that actually works]; He is a shield [magen] over those whose walk is blameless [tom — wholeness, a life with no hidden seam],
7.notes: tsaphan (H6845) binds God's action to the son's: the son treasures up God's words (v.1), and God treasures up tushiyyah (H8454) — sound, success-bringing wisdom — for him. tom (H8537) is integrity, wholeness without a hidden crack. To such a walk God Himself is the magen (H4043), the shield. Other brackets: yashar (H3477).

8.text: guarding the paths of justice and watching over the way of His faithful ones.
8.amp: guarding [natsar — keep watch over] the paths of justice [mishpat] and watching over [shamar — preserve, keep] the way of His faithful ones [chasidim — the covenant-loyal, bound to Him in steadfast love].
8.notes: natsar (H5341) and shamar (H8104) are near-synonyms for sentry-keeping, doubled for assurance. chasid (H2623) is the covenant-faithful one, marked by chesed (steadfast love); God keeps watch over the very road such a man walks. Other brackets: mishpat (H4941).

9.text: Then you will discern righteousness and justice and equity — every good path.
9.amp: Then you will discern [biyn] righteousness [tsedek — right relating], justice [mishpat — right deciding], and equity [meyshar — level, straight dealing] — every good [tov] track [magal].
9.notes: the second 'then' (cf. v.5): the same three-fold moral vocabulary as 1:3 — tsedek (H6664), mishpat (H4941), meyshar (H4339) — now becomes the reader's own discernment. Wisdom received as gift (v.6) becomes wisdom exercised as judgment. Other brackets: biyn (H995), tov (H2896), magal (H4570).

10.text: For wisdom will come into your heart, and knowledge will be a delight to your soul;
10.amp: For wisdom [chokmah] will enter [bo — come in and settle] your heart [leb], and knowledge [daat] will be a delight [naam — be sweet, pleasant] to your soul [nephesh];
10.notes: the turn from acquiring to enjoying: chokmah does not merely inform the head but enters (bo, H935) the leb (H3820), the inner seat of will and affection, until daat becomes naam (H5276) — something the nephesh finds positively sweet. Wisdom is not only obeyed; it is loved.

11.text: discretion will stand watch over you, understanding will guard you,
11.amp: discretion [mezimmah — the planning, foreseeing mind] will stand watch over you [shamar], understanding [tebunah] will guard [natsar] you,
11.notes: mezimmah (H4209) is the power to plan ahead — a 'gray' word that elsewhere serves evil scheming, but here, ruled by wisdom, becomes foresight that protects. The guard-verbs shamar (H8104) and natsar (H5341) carry over from God's keeping in v.8: the wisdom He keeps now keeps the man.

12.text: to rescue you from the way of evil, from the man who speaks twisted things —
12.amp: to rescue you [natsal — snatch you away] from the way of evil [derek ra], from the man who speaks perverse things [tahpukot — twisted, upside-down speech],
12.notes: the first protective purpose of wisdom: natsal (H5337) is a rescue verb, to snatch from danger. tahpukah (H8419) means things turned upside-down — speech that inverts good and evil. The first peril wisdom guards against is the man whose words bend the truth.

13.text: men who abandon the straight paths to walk in the ways of darkness,
13.amp: men who abandon [azab — forsake, let go of] the paths of uprightness [yosher — straightness] to walk [yalak] in the ways of darkness [choshek],
13.notes: azab (H5800), to forsake, marks a deliberate turning: these are not the lost but the leavers, who knew the straight road (yosher, H3476) and chose the dark one. choshek (H2822), darkness, is the moral element they now move in.

14.text: who are glad to do evil and exult in the perversity of evil,
14.amp: who rejoice [sameach — are glad, take pleasure] to do [asah] evil and exult [gil — spin round with joy] in the perversity [tahpukot] of evil,
14.notes: the mark of hardened sin is not reluctance but glee. sameach (H8056) and gil (H1523) are joy-words — the vocabulary of harvest and worship — here bent toward delight in wrong. They have come to love the twist (tahpukah, H8419) for its own sake.

15.text: whose paths are crooked and who are devious in their tracks.
15.amp: whose paths [orach] are crooked [iqqesh — bent, twisted out of true] and who are devious [luz — turning aside, going off the line] in their tracks [magal].
15.notes: iqqesh (H6141), crooked, and luz (H3868), to turn aside, describe a life that no longer runs straight — every step subtly off the true line. The image completes vv.12-14: crooked speech, crooked joy, crooked walk.

16.text: It will rescue you, too, from the forbidden woman, from the smooth-tongued stranger with her flattering words —
16.amp: to rescue you [natsal] also from the forbidden woman [ishshah zarah — the 'strange' woman, outside the bounds of covenant marriage], from the foreigner [nokriyyah] who flatters [chalaq — makes her words smooth and slippery] with her words [emer];
16.notes: the second peril, set in deliberate parallel to v.12: the ishshah zarah (zur, H2114) and nokriyyah (H5237) — 'strange'/'foreign' not by race but by being off-limits, another man's or no man's. chalaq (H2505) is to make smooth: her speech is frictionless, the opposite of wisdom's wholesome but bracing words.

17.text: she who has deserted the partner of her youth and let slip the covenant of her God.
17.amp: she who forsakes [azab — the same abandoning verb as v.13] the companion [alluph — the close friend, the husband of her youth] of her youth [neurim] and forgets [shakach] the covenant [berith] of her God [Elohim].
17.notes: azab (H5800) ties her to the apostates of v.13 — both are forsakers. alluph (H441) is an intimate companion; the 'covenant of her God' (berith, H1285) frames marriage as a vow made before God, so her adultery is covenant-breaking, a small treason against heaven.

18.text: for her house sinks down to death, and her paths to the shades of the departed.
18.amp: for her house [bayith] sinks down [shuach — settles, sags] to death [mavet], and her tracks [magal] to the departed spirits [repaim — the shades, the ghostly dead of the underworld];
18.notes: the seduction's true destination: shuach (H7743), to sink, pictures the whole house tilting downward toward mavet (H4194). repaim (H7496) are the shades of the dead in Sheol — her path ends not in pleasure but in the grave's grey company; cf. 7:27; 9:18.

19.text: Not one who goes in to her ever comes back, nor recovers the road that leads to life.
19.amp: None who go in [bo] to her return [shub — come back, turn around] again, nor do they reach [nasag — overtake, lay hold of] the paths of life [chayyim];
19.notes: shub (H7725), the great repentance-verb, is exactly what her victims fail to do — the road in has no road back. nasag (H5381) is to catch up to, to overtake; they can no longer overtake the orach chayyim (H2416), the paths of life that recede out of reach. The warning is not prudish but mortal.

20.text: Thus the road you walk will be the road of good men, and the tracks you guard, the tracks of the righteous.
20.amp: Thus [the aim of all this rescue] the road [derek] you walk [yalak] will be the road of good [tov] men, and the tracks [orach] you guard [shamar — keep, hold to], the tracks of the righteous [tsaddiqim].
20.notes: the goal of the double rescue (vv.12-19) is not mere escape but direction: kept from the crooked man and the smooth woman, the son is freed to walk the derek of the tov (H2896) and guard (shamar, H8104) the tracks of the tsaddiq (H6662). Wisdom removes from one road in order to set on another.

21.text: For it is the upright who will settle in the land, and the blameless who are left to remain in it;
21.amp: For the upright [yashar] will dwell [shakan — settle, take up lasting residence] in the land [eretz], and the blameless [tamim — whole, without defect] will be left remaining [yathar] in it;
21.notes: shakan (H7931) is settled, abiding dwelling — the root behind the tabernacle (mishkan), where God Himself dwells. To inherit and stay in the eretz (H776) is the covenant blessing (cf. Ps 37:29; Matt 5:5); the tamim (H8549), the whole-hearted, are the ones who endure (yathar, H3498) when the wicked are swept away.

22.text: but the wicked will be cut off from the land, and the treacherous torn away from it.
22.amp: but the wicked [resha'im] will be cut off [karath — severed, the covenant-curse verb] from the land [eretz], and the treacherous [bagad — the faithless, the betrayers] torn away [nasach — plucked up by the roots] from it.
22.notes: the book's first great either/or closes the chapter: karath (H3772) is to cut off — the same verb used for cutting (making) a covenant, here for being severed from the land's blessing. bagad (H898), to deal treacherously, names the perverse man and the adulteress together as covenant-betrayers; nasach (H5255) uproots them like a weed. Two destinies, one land.
